*   Better handling of uneven statistical distributions between intraslice and interslice directions [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that tree-based coders give better performance when the statistical distribution of magnitudes of wavelet coefficients is uneven between intraslice and interslice directions. It further explains that the asymmetric tree structure (AT-SPIHT) is designed to make trees longer, which increases the probability of zero coefficients, thereby improving performance in these specific conditions. The claim accurately reflects this mechanism described in the source.

Asymmetric Tree SPIHT (AT-SPIHT) is a lossless compression method for volumetric medical images (CT/MR) that combines a 3-D reversible integer wavelet transform with a Set Partitioning in Hierarchical Trees (SPIHT) coder operating on an asymmetric tree structure [S1].

The claim states that AT-SPIHT is a lossless compression method for volumetric medical images (CT/MR) combining a 3-D reversible integer wavelet transform with a SPIHT coder on an asymmetric tree structure. The evidence explicitly confirms: 1) It is a 'lossless compression of volumetric medical images' (Source [S1] passages). 2) It applies to 'computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance (MR) images' (Source [S1] passages). 3) It uses '3-D reversible integer wavelet transforms' (Source [S1] passages). 4) It uses the 'set partitioning in hierarchical tree (SPIHT) algorithm that searches on asymmetric trees' (Source [S1] passages). All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported

The evidence explicitly states in the passages that the asymmetric tree structure is 'naturally unbalanced' and that this allows the system to 'decompose to more levels in the transaxial domain than in the axial domain.' This directly supports every part of the claim.

Within each axial sub-band, the tree grows according to standard 2-D SPIHT rules for the remaining coefficients, linking to transaxial sub-bands [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'To grow the tree further, each coefficient group is linked with each transaxial sub-band, the same as with original 2-D SPIHT.' It further details that within the axial sub-bands (LLt, LHt, Ht), the tree grows by linking to offspring groups in the same or subsequent axial sub-bands (e.g., 'each 2 × 2 coefficient group in the lowest transaxial sub-band of the axial LLt band has three 2 × 2 offspring groups in the axial LLt band and one 2 × 2 offspring group in the LHt band'). This confirms that the growth follows standard 2-D SPIHT rules for the remaining coefficients while linking to transaxial sub-bands.
supported
